name: feit_thompson
title: Feit–Thompson theorem
explanation: The full theorem (every odd-order finite group is solvable) requires the entire 255-page Feit-Thompson argument: local analysis classifying maximal subgroups, exceptional/coherent character theory and the Dade isometry, and Thompson's generators-and-relations elimination of the final configuration.

name: friedlander_iwaniec
title: Friedlander--Iwaniec theorem
explanation: Infinitude of primes of the form a^2+b^4 needs Friedlander-Iwaniec's ~100-page parity-sensitive asymptotic sieve for primes, with delicate Type I/II bilinear-form estimates and the 'spin' of Gaussian ideals to handle this density-X^{3/4} sparse sequence.

name: Nat.Prime.greenTao
title: Green–Tao theorem
explanation: The full Green-Tao result requires Szemeredi's theorem (itself a major graduate theorem), a relative/transference Szemeredi theorem against a pseudorandom measure, and the Goldston-Pintz-Yildirim sieve construction enveloping the primes, all of which the formal statement demands in full generality for arbitrary k.

name: robin
title: Robin's theorem
explanation: The formalized statement is the full biconditional with the Riemann Hypothesis, so the reverse direction effectively requires proving RH; even granting that, Robin's 1984 forward analysis uses Gronwall's maximal-order asymptotics, Mertens' third theorem, superabundant/colossally-abundant number theory and explicit zero-free-region estimates for zeta.

name: linnik
title: Linnik's theorem
explanation: The least prime in an arithmetic progression bound requires the full analytic machinery of Linnik's proof: log-free zero-density estimates for Dirichlet L-functions, the Deuring-Heilbronn phenomenon repelling exceptional Siegel zeros, and zero-free regions, the deepest result in the set.

name: szemeredi
title: Szemerédi's Theorem
explanation: The formal statement is the full Szemeredi theorem (positive upper density forces arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions); every known route is deep research-level - Furstenberg's ergodic-theoretic multiple recurrence, Gowers' Fourier analysis with the inverse theorem for Gowers norms, or Szemeredi's regularity lemma - each requiring extensive machinery far beyond undergraduate.

name: two_ninety_theorem
title: The 290 Theorem
explanation: Bhargava-Hanke's proof escalates lattices up to rank 7 (~20000 cases) and certifies universality of the remaining forms via theta-series identities and analytic bounds on Fourier coefficients of cusp forms, requiring substantial modular-forms machinery plus large verified computations.

name: koukoulopoulos_maynard
title: Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture / Koukoulopoulos–Maynard theorem
explanation: This is the full Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture (Koukoulopoulos-Maynard, Annals 2020), whose proof builds the novel combinatorial theory of GCD graphs and their 'quality' combined with the anatomy of integers and sieve theory to rule out compressed/large-GCD structures, an entire research-paper's worth of new machinery.

name: chen
title: Chen's theorem
explanation: The formalized statement is the full Chen's theorem (every sufficiently large even number = prime + (prime or semiprime)), whose proof is a celebrated, long and intricate application of the weighted (Chen's double) sieve combined with the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions and Jurkat-Richert-type sieve bounds, well beyond undergraduate analytic number theory even in Ross's simplified form.

name: farey_riemann_abs
title: Farey Sequence
explanation: Formalizes the full Franel-Landau equivalence (an iff) between RH and the L^1 discrepancy bound on Farey fractions, which requires both directions of the deep analytic-number-theory link (Mellin/Perron-type transforms and the explicit-formula apparatus connecting Farey discrepancy to zeros of zeta), making it as demanding as developing the surrounding zeta-function machinery.

name: mergelyan
title: Mergelyan's theorem
explanation: Uniform polynomial approximation on compacts with connected complement requires the deep constructive machinery of Mergelyan/Vitushkin: Cauchy-transform integral representations, smoothing via partitions of unity, continuity of analytic capacity, and Runge-type pole-pushing, well beyond undergraduate complex analysis.

name: roth
title: Roth's theorem
explanation: Full Thue-Siegel-Roth theorem (irrationality measure exactly 2 for algebraic irrationals), whose proof needs the auxiliary-multivariate-polynomial method, Siegel's lemma from geometry of numbers, and Roth's lemma on the index/Wronskians of polynomials proved by induction on the number of variables.

name: cameron_erdos
title: Cameron–Erdős conjecture
explanation: Proving the number of sum-free subsets of [n] is O(2^{n/2}) requires either Green's discrete Fourier analysis with the hypergraph container method or Sapozhenko's Kleitman-Winston/graph-container approach, a substantial body of modern additive-combinatorics research machinery.

name: KroneckerWeber
title: Kronecker–Weber theorem
explanation: The formalized statement is the full Kronecker-Weber theorem (every abelian extension of Q lies in a cyclotomic field), whose proof requires either global class field theory (Artin reciprocity) or the ramification-group approach reducing to the local Kronecker-Weber theorem plus Minkowski's discriminant bound, all substantial graduate algebraic number theory.

name: fifteen_theorem
title: The 15 Theorem
explanation: The integer-symmetric-matrix (even) form of the 15 theorem needs Bhargava's escalator-lattice induction together with the arithmetic theory of ternary/quaternary positive-definite quadratic forms (local representability, genus theory, and case analysis over the escalator tree), substantial graduate quadratic-form machinery.

name: Freiman
title: Freiman's Theorem
explanation: The full structure theorem requires the chain of additive-combinatorics machinery: Plunnecke-Ruzsa inequalities, the Ruzsa modeling lemma via Freiman homomorphisms, Bogolyubov's lemma with Fourier analysis on Bohr sets, and Minkowski's geometry-of-numbers to extract a bounded-dimension generalized arithmetic progression.

name: brunTitchmarsh
title: Brun–Titchmarsh theorem
explanation: The sharp constant-2 bound on primes in an arithmetic progression in a short interval requires the Montgomery-Vaughan large sieve (or Selberg's sieve with the bilinear error analysis), substantial analytic number theory machinery well beyond undergraduate level.

name: gelfond_scheider
title: Gelfond–Schneider theorem
explanation: Gelfond-Schneider's seventh-Hilbert-problem proof builds an auxiliary function via the Thue-Siegel-Dirichlet box principle (Siegel's lemma over algebraic integers), bounds its derivatives/values using complex-analytic interpolation and the maximum modulus principle, and derives a contradiction from arithmetic size (house) estimates; this transcendence machinery is well beyond undergraduate, though the formalized statement is garbled (it asserts the algebraic b is transcendental).

name: HasseBound
title: Hasse's theorem on elliptic curves
explanation: Hasse's bound follows from showing the degree map on End(E) is a positive-definite quadratic form and applying Cauchy-Schwarz to the Frobenius-related pairing, but developing the elliptic-curve group law over finite fields, the Frobenius endomorphism, separability/degree of isogenies, and #E = deg(1-Frob) is substantial graduate arithmetic geometry.

name: erdos_kac
title: Erdős–Kac theorem
explanation: Establishes the full normal-distribution limit law via the method of moments (Granville-Soundararajan style) or the original Brun-sieve-plus-Lindeberg-CLT argument, requiring graduate analytic number theory (mean values of additive functions, sieve error control) well beyond the undergraduate CLT it superficially resembles.

name: grushko
title: Grushko theorem
explanation: Grushko's theorem on the rank of a free product is proved either via Stallings' equivariant foldings of group actions on covering complexes/trees or via Bass-Serre theory and graphs of groups, both requiring graduate geometric group theory and algebraic topology beyond the undergraduate curriculum.

name: apery
title: Apery
explanation: Full irrationality of zeta(3) is formalized, requiring Apery's delicate construction of two integer-recurrence sequences (Apery numbers), nontrivial control of the lcm-denominators to keep them near-integral, and a Diophantine-approximation irrationality criterion, all of which take substantial graduate-level development to make rigorous.

name: jordan_schur
title: Jordan–Schur theorem
explanation: Even though the formalized statement only asks for existence of some bounding function f(n) (no explicit bound), establishing it still needs the full Frobenius-Blichfeldt argument using character theory and a quantitative bound on commutators of near-identity unitary matrices, which is substantial graduate group-representation machinery.

name: brun
title: Brun's theorem
explanation: Requires Brun's combinatorial sieve (his 'pure sieve', a truncated inclusion-exclusion) to bound the twin-prime counting function by O(x/log^2 x), from which summability follows; developing the sieve machinery and the careful error-term estimates is the bulk of the work, beyond standard undergraduate number theory.

name: critical_line
title: Critical Line Theorem
explanation: The statement is exactly Hardy's 1914 theorem (infinitely many zeta zeros on Re(s)=1/2), proved via Hardy's Z-function and the theta/Jacobi transformation formula together with the approximate functional equation and integral/moment estimates of Z(t), requiring genuine analytic number theory beyond a basic complex analysis course.

name: kaplansky_two
title: Kaplansky's theorem on quadratic forms
explanation: This 2003 result combines Gauss's quartic-residue criterion (2 is a 4th power mod p iff p = x^2+64y^2) and the Barrucand-Cohn octic criterion (-4 is an 8th power iff p = x^2+32y^2) with genus theory of binary quadratic forms and higher reciprocity, requiring well beyond undergraduate number theory.

name: lukacs_proportion_sum_independence_iff
title: Lukacs's proportion-sum independence theorem
explanation: The hard (only-if) direction is a characterization theorem proved via Laplace transforms/characteristic functions reduced to a Cauchy-type functional equation forcing the gamma law, requiring graduate mathematical-statistics machinery plus the measure-theoretic setup of HasLaw and the gamma measure.

name: waring
title: Waring's Problem
explanation: The formalized statement only asserts existence of a uniform bound t (the Hilbert-Waring theorem), proved by Hilbert via algebraic polynomial identities (the Hilbert identity expressing power-sum integrals as sums of k-th powers) and an induction; clever and several pages beyond undergraduate but far easier than determining g(n) via the circle method.

name: zsigmondy_theorem
title: Zsigmondy's theorem
explanation: The proof factors a^n - b^n via homogeneous cyclotomic polynomials Phi_n(a,b), shows any primitive prime divides Phi_n, then uses multiplicative-order arguments plus the Lifting-the-Exponent lemma (Birkhoff-Vandiver) and analytic lower bounds on Phi_n(a,b) to force a contradiction, with delicate separate handling of the n=2 power-of-two and (a,b,n)=(2,1,6) exceptions; the formalized statement is the full general theorem with both exceptions, requiring substantial cyclotomic-polynomial and p-adic-valuation machinery beyond undergraduate number theory.

name: Jacobson_Morozov
title: Jacobson-Morozov Theorem
explanation: Driven by graduate structure theory of semisimple Lie algebras: an induction on dimension using the Killing form, representation theory of sl2, and a cohomological/centralizer argument to extend a nilpotent ad-nilpotent element to a full sl2-triple.

name: NagellLutz2
title: Nagell–Lutz theorem
explanation: Full theorem driven by graduate elliptic-curve machinery: p-adic valuations / the formal group filtration on E1(Qp) and reduction mod p to bound torsion, plus the discriminant-divisibility (y^2 | Delta) step, all of which must be developed beyond undergraduate algebra.

name: aztecDiamond_tiling
title: Aztec-Diamonds
explanation: The full count 2^(n(n+1)/2) for all n is formalized; even the 'simple' proofs require real machinery such as the Lindstrom-Gessel-Viennot lemma with Hankel/Schroder-number determinant evaluations, or the domino-shuffling/field-of-arrows induction, none of which is standard undergraduate material.

name: EuclideanSpace.volume_pow_add_le
title: Brunn-Minkowski Inequality (Additive Form)
explanation: The additive Brunn-Minkowski inequality in general dimension n needs either the Hadwiger-Ohmann induction through boxes/finite unions plus measure-theoretic limiting arguments, or the Prekopa-Leindler functional approach with induction on dimension via Fubini; conceptually graduate-level measure theory and convex geometry.

name: EuclideanSpace.volume_pow_mul_le
title: Brunn-Minkowski Inequality (Multiplicative Form)
explanation: The multiplicative (dimension-free-exponent) form is equivalent to the additive Brunn-Minkowski via weighted AM-GM, so it carries the same Prekopa-Leindler/Hadwiger-Ohmann machinery and induction-on-dimension burden as the additive version.

name: carmichael
title: Carmichael's theorem
explanation: Establishing a primitive prime divisor for Lucas sequences U_n (n outside {1,2,6,12}) uses factorization via cyclotomic polynomials Phi_n at the roots, lower bounds on cyclotomic values versus the radical of n, and Yabuta's reduction to Fibonacci/Fermat sequences; technical elementary number theory beyond standard coursework.

name: diller_dress
title: Diller–Dress theorem
explanation: The going-down of the Pythagorean property under finite extensions rests on the algebraic theory of quadratic forms over fields, specifically Scharlau transfer (trace forms) and Witt-ring arguments controlling sums of squares, which is graduate-level quadratic-form theory not in the standard undergraduate algebra curriculum.

name: picard
title: Picard theorem
explanation: Little Picard theorem: the formalized 'omits two values implies constant' statement still needs either the elliptic modular lambda covering of the twice-punctured plane or the Bloch/Landau-theorem route, machinery well beyond a basic complex-analysis course.

name: polygonal_number_theorem_odd
title: Polygonal Number Theorem (Odd Case)
explanation: Nathanson's proof of the odd case rests on Cauchy's lemma producing a four-square representation with prescribed root-sum, which in turn invokes Gauss's three-square theorem (genus theory / ternary quadratic forms), the main source of difficulty beyond undergraduate number theory.

name: ramanujan_nagell
title: Ramanujan–Nagell equation
explanation: Nagell's proof factors 2^n - 7 = x^2 in the ring of integers of Q(sqrt(-7)) using unique factorization and the unit group {+-1}, then a recurrence/2-adic argument forces n in {3,4,5,7,15}; the algebraic-number-theory setup (class number one, factorization in Z[(1+sqrt(-7))/2]) is the graduate-level core.

name: tverberg
title: Tverberg's theorem
explanation: The formalized statement is the full affine Tverberg theorem for all d,r; Sarkaria's proof uses a tensor/Kronecker-product lifting reducing it to the colorful Caratheodory theorem (Barany), a compact but conceptually nontrivial argument with the colorful Caratheodory lemma itself needing proof.

name: anderson
title: Anderson's theorem
explanation: The general n-dimensional statement is formalized; the standard proof goes through the Brunn-Minkowski inequality applied to convex superlevel sets (the layer-cake decomposition of the unimodal f), which is genuine graduate convex-geometry machinery rather than a one-dimensional rearrangement.

name: borsuk_ulam
title: Borsuk–Ulam theorem
explanation: The full S^n version is formalized; the proof needs algebraic-topology machinery (degree theory or Z/2 homology/cohomology of projective spaces with the Hurewicz and universal-coefficient theorems), or alternatively the combinatorial Tucker's lemma, all requiring development well beyond undergraduate topology.

name: jacobi
title: Jacobi's Four-Square Theorem
explanation: The classical proof represents the number of four-square representations via the fourth power of the Jacobi theta function and identifies it with an Eisenstein series / Lambert series using the Jacobi triple product and theta-function identities, which is doable elementarily but requires several pages of theta-function machinery beyond undergraduate analysis.

name: SchauderFixedPointTheorem
title: Schauder fixed-point theorem
explanation: Infinite-dimensional fixed-point theorem reducing to Brouwer's fixed-point theorem via finite-dimensional approximation by a partition-of-unity (Schauder projection) onto convex hulls of finite epsilon-nets in the compact convex set of a locally convex TVS.

name: beckmann_quarles
title: Beckman–Quarles theorem
explanation: The genuine theorem (d>=2) relies on the structural rigidity of unit-distance graphs, e.g. propagating preserved unit distances through rigid simplex configurations to a dense set of distances; note the formal statement omits the d>=2 hypothesis so it is actually false for d=1 where a unit-shift counterexample exists, but the hard mathematical content is the rigidity argument.

name: carlson
title: Carlson's theorem
explanation: The proof divides f by the sine function (whose zeros are the integers) and applies the Phragmen-Lindelof principle in a half-plane, using the exponential-type bound and the sub-pi growth on the imaginary axis to force the quotient to vanish; intermediate complex analysis a step beyond the undergraduate core.

name: erdos_dushnik_miller
title: Erdős–Dushnik–Miller theorem
explanation: This infinite partition relation (clique of size |V| or a countably infinite independent set) requires transfinite recursion over cardinals and a tree/elementary-submodel style argument in infinitary combinatorics, genuinely set-theoretic machinery beyond undergraduate combinatorics.

name: tauberian
title: Hardy–Littlewood Tauberian theorem
explanation: Karamata's elegant proof reduces the Tauberian statement to approximating a step function by polynomials (Weierstrass approximation) applied to the positive-coefficient series, using essentially only real analysis but with a genuinely non-obvious approximation argument slightly above routine undergraduate work.

name: kolmogorov_three_series_necessity
title: Kolmogorov's Three Series, necessity
explanation: The necessity direction is the harder one, requiring Kolmogorov's inequality/two-series theorem and a symmetrization plus martingale (or CLT-type) variance argument to deduce the truncated variance and mean series converge, all in measure-theoretic probability beyond undergraduate level.

name: totient_lower_bound
title: Lower bound on totient growth
explanation: The explicit bound phi(n) > n/(e^gamma loglog n + 3/loglog n) rests on Mertens' third theorem (product over primes ~ e^{-gamma}/log x) plus Chebyshev-type estimates and careful error control, modestly beyond the standard undergraduate analytic-number-theory toolkit.

name: sinkhorn_existence
title: Sinkhorn's theorem
explanation: Existence of diagonal scalings to doubly stochastic form, proved via a compactness/continuity or convex-optimization (entropy minimization) argument on positive matrices, beyond routine undergraduate material but using only finite-dimensional analysis.

name: two_factor_theorem
title: 2-factor theorem
explanation: Petersen's proof orients the graph via an Eulerian circuit to get an in/out-degree-k digraph, then splits each vertex into a k-regular bipartite graph and decomposes it into k perfect matchings by Konig's theorem - standard advanced-undergraduate graph theory.

name: banach_mazur
title: Banach-Mazur Theorem
explanation: The full separable case is formalized; the proof embeds the space into C[0,1] (via C of the weak-* compact, metrizable dual unit ball plus a Peano space-filling surjection) using Hahn-Banach and weak-* compactness, which is graduate functional analysis beyond the undergraduate core.

name: brooks_theorem
title: Brooks' theorem
explanation: Formalizes the full classification; Lovasz's proof is upper-undergraduate combinatorics but genuinely involved, requiring a biconnectivity reduction, a careful greedy ordering via a spanning tree rooted to leave a neighbor uncolored, and special-case handling of the regular biconnected case.

name: caristi
title: Caristi fixed-point theorem
explanation: The proof builds a partial order x <= y iff dist(x,y) <= f(x)-f(y) and applies Zorn's lemma (using completeness and lower semicontinuity) to extract a minimal element that must be a fixed point; a short argument using graduate-flavored but elementary order/metric reasoning.

name: ErdosGallaiTheorem
title: Erdős–Gallai theorem
explanation: The full characterization of graphical degree sequences (the iff) needs the harder existence direction, established by induction on the degree sum (Choudum) or a subrealization/edge-swapping construction (Tripathi et al.); this is involved but elementary graph theory, the constructive realization being the main work.

name: fitting
title: Fitting's theorem
explanation: A standard graduate group-theory result proved by commutator calculus and the three-subgroups lemma to bound the nilpotency class of MN by m+n; short once the commutator identities and lower-central-series bookkeeping are set up.

name: hurwitz_approximation
title: Hurwitz's Approximation Theorem
explanation: Hurwitz's approximation theorem is proved through the theory of continued fractions (showing one of three consecutive convergents satisfies the sqrt5 bound) or via Farey/mediant arguments, standard elementary number theory but requiring the somewhat involved convergent-comparison machinery.

name: kolmogorov_three_series_sufficiency
title: Kolmogorov's Three Series, sufficiency
explanation: The sufficiency direction follows from Kolmogorov's two-series theorem (via Kolmogorov's maximal inequality) on the centered truncated variables plus Borel-Cantelli to pass back to the original series, requiring graduate-level measure-theoretic probability machinery.

name: LeCamTheorem
title: Le Cam's theorem
explanation: The formalized bound (total variation of a sum of independent Bernoullis from Poisson <= 2 sum p_i^2) is proved by a coupling/Serfling argument bounding each Bernoulli-vs-Poisson term, modest graduate probability beyond undergraduate measure-theoretic probability.

name: levitzky_theorem
title: Levitzky's theorem
explanation: Utumi's argument uses the ascending chain condition (here Noetherian on the opposite ring) to extract a maximal nilpotent ideal and reduce to a semiprime quotient, requiring graduate noncommutative ring theory on nil versus nilpotent ideals.

name: lusin
title: Lusin's theorem
explanation: Standard real-analysis proof via approximating the measurable function by simple/continuous functions, Egorov's theorem to upgrade to near-uniform convergence, and an inner-regularity/Tietze extension step; modest material slightly beyond a first measure theory course.

name: prekopa_leindler_dim1
title: Main Theorem: Prékopa-Leindler inequality in dimension 1
explanation: The 1D case has a short proof via a measure-transport/level-set (essential-supremum convolution) argument with the layer-cake formula and a Brunn-Minkowski-type 1D length bound; only modestly beyond undergraduate measure theory.

name: merten_first
title: Mertens' First Theorem
explanation: Elementary analytic number theory: Legendre's formula for v_p(n!), Stirling's estimate for log(n!), and Abel partial summation give the bounded-difference estimate; mostly within reach of undergraduate analysis but requires assembling these prime-power summation arguments.

name: mycielski
title: Mycielski's theorem
explanation: Requires iterating the Mycielskian construction and proving by induction that it stays triangle-free (K3-free) while raising the chromatic number by one via a recoloring/contradiction argument; the formalized statement is just the existence direction, but building the construction and the chromatic-number lower bound in a proof assistant is non-trivial combinatorics.

name: sinkhorn_uniqueness
title: Sinkhorn's theorem
explanation: Uniqueness (up to the scalar c) of the diagonal scalings, established by a strict-convexity/log-convexity argument on the positive scaling factors showing two doubly-stochastic scalings must differ only by the stated reciprocal constant.

name: szemeredi_trotter
title: Szemerédi–Trotter theorem
explanation: Szekely's proof builds a planar graph from points and line-segments and applies the crossing-number inequality (itself from Euler's formula plus a probabilistic deletion argument), a short and clever advanced-undergraduate combinatorial-geometry argument.

name: wolstenholme
title: Wolstenholme's theorem
explanation: Wolstenholme's mod-p^3 congruence follows from manipulating C(2p-1,p-1) into 1 + p*(harmonic-type sum) and showing the relevant Wolstenholme harmonic sums vanish mod p^2 via pairing/inversion arguments in the cyclic group, a few pages of elementary-but-careful number theory.

name: bauer_fike
title: Bauer–Fike Theorem
explanation: A standard diagonalizable-matrix eigenvalue perturbation bound whose roughly two-thirds-page proof is a similarity transformation plus a subordinate-matrix-norm/condition-number estimate, essentially advanced undergraduate linear algebra with only a thin layer of perturbation-theory machinery.

name: bondy
title: Bondy's theorem
explanation: A short extremal-combinatorics result (drop one column from an n-by-n 0-1 matrix with distinct rows keeping rows distinct) provable by a linear-algebra dimension/rank argument over GF(2) or a direct counting induction, only modestly beyond the undergraduate core.

name: cartan_brauer_hua
title: Cartan–Brauer–Hua theorem
explanation: Despite its fame, the proof is a short consequence of Hua's identity showing the invariant subfield is fixed; only basic division-ring algebra is needed once the identity is in hand, essentially undergraduate-to-early-graduate.

name: ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_map_of_forall_continuousAt
title: Continuous Mapping Theorem (convergence in distribution version)
explanation: The convergence-in-distribution version requires the portmanteau theorem and careful handling of the discontinuity set having limit-measure zero (weak convergence machinery), modestly beyond a first probability course but standard graduate measure-theoretic probability.

name: frank_wolfe_convergence_rate
title: Convergence rate of Frank-Wolfe algorithm
explanation: The O(1/k) convergence bound follows from the smoothness (descent) lemma giving a per-step decrease via the curvature/duality gap and a simple induction on the optimality gap; essentially advanced-undergraduate convex optimization.

name: SimpleGraph.colorable_of_finitely_colorable
title: De Bruijn-Erd\H{o}s Theorem (Graph Coloring)
explanation: The De Bruijn-Erdos compactness theorem follows from a short topological compactness argument (Tychonoff on the product of finite color spaces) or equivalently Zorn's lemma / the ultrafilter lemma, a modest use of the axiom of choice slightly beyond standard undergraduate topology.

name: dilworth
title: Dilworth's Theorem
explanation: The finite Dilworth theorem has a clean induction proof (Galvin) or a reduction to Konig's bipartite matching/Hall's theorem; it is elementary combinatorics but the chain-partition construction and case analysis push it slightly past trivial.

name: hinge_iff_geometric
title: Hinge Theorem
explanation: This geometric (metric-space) version of the hinge/SAS-inequality requires deriving the law of cosines from the distance/angle structure and the monotonicity of cosine, modestly above the bare algebraic version but still elementary undergraduate Euclidean geometry.

name: koebe
title: Koebe quarter theorem
explanation: A compact complex-analysis proof: the Gronwall area theorem gives Bieberbach's bound |a2| <= 2 for normalized univalent functions, and applying it to the auxiliary function w f/(w-f) yields the 1/4 radius bound; only a couple of pages beyond standard undergraduate complex analysis.

name: proth
title: Proth's theorem
explanation: A special case of the Pocklington-Lehmer test (like Pepin's test): the converse and forward directions follow from Euler's criterion and order-of-element arguments mod n for n = k*2^m+1, essentially elementary number theory.

name: schur
title: Schur's theorem
explanation: Short combinatorial pigeonhole/Ramsey argument: apply Ramsey's theorem to the complete graph colored by edge differences to get a monochromatic triangle yielding x+y=z, requiring development of finite Ramsey's theorem.

name: starofdavid
title: Star of David
explanation: Elementary number theory: prove the two triples of binomial coefficients have equal gcd by factorial manipulation of the Star-of-David hexagon identity, with care over the natural-number edge cases (k=0, n=0) in the formal statement.

name: vantieghem
title: Vantieghem's Theorem
explanation: This primality criterion is proved from properties of cyclotomic polynomials over F_2 (or, for the 'if' direction, just Fermat's little theorem and elementary congruences), a short self-contained number-theory argument near the undergraduate level.

name: von_staudt_clausen
title: Von Staudt-Clausen Theorem
explanation: The classical proof expresses Bernoulli numbers via Stirling-number/binomial sums and uses Fermat's little theorem to evaluate power sums mod p, distinguishing whether p-1 divides 2n - entirely elementary modular arithmetic with only modest mileage beyond undergraduate.

name: SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.berge
title: Berge's theorem
explanation: A standard undergraduate graph-theory result proved by analyzing the symmetric difference of two matchings into alternating paths and even cycles; the only effort is the component-structure lemma, requiring essentially no machinery beyond the undergraduate level.

name: casorati_weierstrass
title: Casorati-Weierstrass
explanation: Standard undergraduate complex analysis: assume the image misses a neighborhood of some value b, form the bounded holomorphic g=1/(f-b), apply Riemann's removable-singularity theorem, and derive that the singularity is not essential, a contradiction; a one-paragraph proof.

name: condorcet_jury_theorem
title: Condorcet's Jury Theorem
explanation: Fully elementary: the monotonicity in n follows from a short pivotal-voter/binomial-tail comparison (the (1-p)p^2 vs p(1-p)^2 argument) using only basic probability and combinatorics at the undergraduate level.

name: ae_tendsto_comp_of_ae_tendsto_of_forall_continuousAt
title: Continuous Mapping Theorem (almost sure convergence version)
explanation: This is the almost-sure version, which is a few-line measure-theoretic argument intersecting two almost-sure events (continuity at the limit point and pointwise convergence) and applying the definition of continuity, entirely undergraduate measure theory.

name: Real.countable_not_continuousAt
title: Froda's Theorem
explanation: Elementary undergraduate real analysis: each jump discontinuity of a monotone function contains a distinct rational between its one-sided limits, injecting the discontinuity set into the countable rationals.

name: Complex.mem_convexHull_roots_of_mem_derivative_roots
title: Gauss-Lucas
explanation: Undergraduate-level: the logarithmic-derivative identity P'(z)/P(z)=sum 1/(z-a_i) at a root of P' rearranges into an explicit positive convex combination of the roots, placing z in their convex hull.

name: hinge_backward
title: Hinge Theorem with Law of Cosines, Backward
explanation: The converse direction is again pure algebra using the supplied cosine equations and strict monotonicity of cosine on [0,pi], entirely undergraduate.

name: hinge_forward
title: Hinge Theorem with Law of Cosines, Forward
explanation: Given the two law-of-cosines equations as hypotheses, this reduces to algebra plus the monotonic decrease of cosine on [0,pi], fully elementary undergraduate real analysis.

name: Module.End.inv_eigenvalue_iff
title: Inverse Eigenvalue Theorem
explanation: Despite the 'inverse eigenvalue problem' title, the formalized statement is merely the trivial fact that r is an eigenvalue of an invertible map iff r^-1 is an eigenvalue of the inverse, a one-line linear-algebra computation on eigenvectors.

name: jones
title: Jones' Lemma
explanation: A short cardinal-counting argument: each subset of the discrete closed set has disjoint open neighborhoods by normality, and restricting closures of these to a countable dense set injects the power set of Y into the continuum, using only point-set topology and basic cardinal arithmetic.

name: kraft
title: Kraft
explanation: An entirely elementary combinatorial construction: sort the lengths and greedily assign codewords as nodes of an r-ary tree (or via the radix-point partial-sum construction), with the Kraft inequality guaranteeing a free node always remains; fully undergraduate.

name: krull_separation
title: Krull's separation lemma
explanation: A direct Zorn's lemma argument producing an ideal maximal among those disjoint from the multiplicative set and showing it is prime, entirely within undergraduate commutative algebra.

name: lagrange
title: Lagrange's theorem (number theory)
explanation: Elementary induction on the degree using polynomial division by (x-k) over the field Z/pZ, fully undergraduate number theory.

name: mcmillan
title: McMillan
explanation: Karush's counting argument: raise the Kraft sum to the m-th power, bound the count of length-l strings using unique decodability, then take m-th roots and let m->infinity, fully elementary combinatorics.

name: ore_maximal_hamiltonian_cycle_free_graph
title: Ore's theorem
explanation: Purely elementary extremal graph argument on an edge-maximal non-Hamiltonian graph (the standard degree-sum lemma at the heart of Ore's theorem), fully undergraduate combinatorics.

name: ore_theorem
title: Ore's theorem
explanation: Classic short extremal/contradiction proof (maximal non-Hamiltonian graph, longest-path rotation, pigeonhole on the degree condition); entirely undergraduate-level graph theory.

name: riemann_summation_atbot
title: Riemann series theorem
explanation: Elementary undergraduate real-analysis greedy-rearrangement construction (alternately accumulate positive/negative terms), here specialized to the easier divergence-to-negative-infinity case rather than the full rearrangement-to-any-value statement.

name: risingsun
title: Rising Sun Lemma
explanation: Purely undergraduate real-analysis argument: openness of the shadow set plus a proof-by-contradiction about maxima of a continuous function, then decomposing an open subset of R into countably many disjoint intervals.

name: rouche_capelli
title: Rouché--Capelli
explanation: Standard undergraduate linear algebra: row-reduce the augmented matrix and compare ranks of coefficient and augmented matrices, an inconsistency 0=1 appearing exactly when the ranks differ.

name: worpitzky
title: Worpitzky identity
explanation: A standard combinatorial identity provable by induction/finite differences on the recurrence A(n,k) = (k+1)A(n-1,k) + (n-k)A(n-1,k-1) for Eulerian numbers together with the binomial Pascal/Vandermonde identities; entirely undergraduate combinatorics, and the formalized statement is the full general identity for all n.
